chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Every eye will weep on the Day of Resurrection, except for three: An eye that stayed awake in the way of Allah, and an eye that overflowed from fear of Allah, and an eye that was restrained from the prohibitions of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the three eyes that will not weep on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the physical manifestation of spiritual states on the Day of Judgment, where the eyes weep in regret except for those preserved through specific acts of worship. This triad emphasizes the holistic nature of piety in Shia tradition, linking active devotion (sahar), internal reverence (khushu'), and sensory restraint (ghadd) as the primary defenses against divine reckoning. The hadith serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate mindfulness in both their worship and their daily interactions with the world.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Every eye will weep on the Day of Judgement apart from three – The eye that stayed awake in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the eye that overflowed from fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the eye that was closed from the Prohibition of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘

On the Day of Judgment all eyes will be weeping except three kinds of eyes: the eye that spends the night awake in the way of Allah, the eye that weeps in submission before Allah and the eye that turns away from what Allah has made unlawful to look at.’”
